papers.title_in_file: Connecting ansatz expressibility to gradient magnitudes and barren plateaus
papers.version_note: arXiv:2101.02138v2 (29 Mar 2022); the record names the PRX Quantum 2022 publication of the same paper.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper with numerics that upper-bounds the variance of the cost gradient of a layered parameterized quantum circuit in terms of the ansatz's distance from a 2-design (its expressibility), extending the barren plateau result to arbitrary ansatze.

existing.certainty_reason: Section IV Discussion and footnote 2 state both limits.

existing.value: The authors report that their numerics typically showed a strong correlation, especially for local cost functions, between expressibility and the variance of the gradient, and that the bounds are not perfectly tight, which they say may arise from the repeated use of the triangle and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities in the derivation; they report the correlation is weaker for global costs.

The correlation is weaker in the case of global costs

existing.note: The bounds are upper bounds only. The paper states that inexpressive ansatze can also show vanishing gradients and that the bounds leave open how reducing expressibility changes the landscape, so the flatter-landscape reading applies to highly expressive ansatze and does not imply that inexpressive ones train well.
existing.value: The authors state that their resulting bounds indicate highly expressive ansatze exhibit flatter cost landscapes and will be harder to train; they also state that the bounds are upper bounds, that highly inexpressive ansatze need not have large gradients and may also have vanishing gradients, and that the bounds leave open how reducing expressibility changes the cost landscape.

assertions.value: The paper defines a barren plateau as gradients that vanish exponentially with the number of qubits, typically relaxed to a probabilistic definition that follows from the Chebyshev inequality if the variance of the partial derivative vanishes exponentially.

assertions.value: The authors restate an earlier cited result that if the left or right part of the circuit forms a 2-design, the variance of the gradient vanishes exponentially in the number of qubits, so maximally expressive ansatze exhibit barren plateaus.

assertions.value: The authors report that correlating both qubits and layers gives the least expressive ansatz and an approximately constant gradient variance, while correlating only qubits or only layers increases gradients and reduces the scaling but an exponential scaling is still observed, with similar results for local and global costs.

papers.what_it_is: A short game-theoretic paper that models an attacker distorting n repeated quantum states seen by a passive (naive) quantum hypothesis-testing detector, derives a worst-case asymptotic miss-rate exponent under separability and norm-bounded attacks, and illustrates it on a conceptual quantum radar case.

existing.certainty_reason: An empirical (numerical) result from one study.

existing.note: Theorem 1 needs more than separable attacker strategies: Lemma 1's eigenvector condition, the same distortion on every copy, and Assumption 1 (local robustness, a diamond-norm tolerance). The paper states that separability alone cannot give a non-vacuous bound. The theorem characterizes the miss-rate exponent, not an average error; the text layer lost its inequality sign and tolerance symbol.
existing.value: The authors derive (Theorem 1) a worst-case asymptotic exponent for the miss rate of the passive detector, as minus an infimum of quantum relative entropy over distorted states within a Wasserstein-distance tolerance, under the assumptions that the attacker's optimal strategy is separable (Lemma 1), that the same distortion is applied to every copy, and that the attacker's operations are locally robust within a diamond-norm tolerance (Assumption 1); they state that separability alone cannot guarantee a bound, since an unconstrained attacker could make the detection rate arbitrarily small.
